title: Microsoft's Agent Benchmark Grades the Database, Not the Transcript
caption:
I've been shipping agents off the strength of a transcript that reads well.

Microsoft's ThinkingBox-Bench doesn't care what the agent says it did. 507 tasks across retail, travel, auto insurance, neobank and IT support — and a task passes only if the final backend state matches a golden state on a hash check. Side effects count. No partial credit.

My demo agent would fail most of these and still sound confident about it.

How do you test yours?

slides.headline:
Nice summary.
Wrong database.
slides.sub: Microsoft's ThinkingBox-Bench scores agents on the final backend state — not on what the agent says it did.

slides.title: Tools are MCP servers
slides.sub: Every task runs in its own isolated, stateful tool session behind a session proxy, driven by a simulated user.

slides.title: How a task passes
items: Final backend state must match a golden state.
Deterministic hash checks. No partial credit.
Side effects count, not just the reply.
30 tasks add yes/no rubrics, judged by an LLM.

slides.headline:
Grade the state.
Not the transcript.
slides.sub: and I'll send the ThinkingBox-Bench run notes
